name: Louvre
places: Salle des États (Mona Lisa room), Louvre Museum
description: The former royal palace turned art museum, entered through a glass pyramid. Its collection runs from ancient Egypt to the Mona Lisa.

name: Musée d’Orsay
description: A museum in a former railway station on the Left Bank, with the largest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist painting.

name: Palais Garnier
description: The 19th-century opera house, with a grand marble staircase and a ceiling painted by Chagall. It hosts opera and ballet.

name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
description: The Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité, reopened in 2024 after the 2019 fire. A plaque in the square marks the point distances in France are measured from.

name: Eiffel Tower
description: The wrought-iron tower built for the 1889 World’s Fair, with lifts and stairs up to viewing platforms over the city.

name: Palace of Versailles
description: The vast palace and gardens of Louis XIV, outside Paris, with the Hall of Mirrors and the royal apartments.

name: Musée de l’Orangerie
description: A small museum in the Tuileries Garden, built around two oval rooms that hold Monet’s Water Lilies panels.

name: Centre Pompidou
description: France’s national museum of modern art, in a 1977 building with its pipes, ducts and escalators on the outside.

name: Le Meurice
places: Le Meurice hotel, Rue de Rivoli
description: A luxury hotel on the Rue de Rivoli facing the Tuileries. During the Occupation it was the headquarters of the German military command in Paris.

name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
places: Édith Piaf’s grave, Père Lachaise Cemetery
description: The city’s largest cemetery, on a hill in the east, with Édith Piaf’s grave and the wall where the last Communards were shot in 1871.

name: Place de la Concorde
places: Luxor Obelisk, Place de la Concorde
description: The largest square in Paris, where the guillotine stood during the Revolution. At its centre is an Egyptian obelisk over 3,000 years old.

name: Place de la Bastille
description: The square where the Bastille prison stood until it was stormed in 1789. A column marks the centre, and traces of the fortress survive in the Métro station.

name: Place du Trocadéro
description: A square across the river from the Eiffel Tower, with terraces that give one of the classic views of it.

name: Shakespeare and Company
description: An English-language bookshop on the Left Bank, across the river from Notre-Dame, crammed with new and second-hand books.

name: Pont des Arts
description: A footbridge across the Seine between the Louvre and the Institut de France, once covered in love padlocks.

name: Pont Neuf
description: Despite its name (‘New Bridge’), the oldest standing bridge across the Seine in Paris, finished in 1607 across the tip of the Île de la Cité.

name: Carnavalet Museum
description: The free museum of the history of Paris, in two mansions in the Marais, with old shop signs, period rooms and relics of the Revolution.

name: Folies Bergère
description: A music hall open since 1869 and famous for its cabaret revues. It now mostly hosts concerts and musicals.

name: Les Invalides
description: Louis XIV’s military hospital under a gilded dome. It now holds Napoleon’s tomb, the army museum and a museum of scale models of fortified towns.

name: Hôtel de Ville
description: Paris’s city hall, a 19th-century rebuilding of a Renaissance original, and the square in front, where public executions once took place.
